examples: We were fortunate enough to find a parking spot right in front of the theater.
ما به‌قدری خوش‌شانس بودیم که جای پارکی درست مقابل سینما پیدا کردیم.
It was fortunate that she brought an umbrella, because it started raining heavily that afternoon.
خوش‌شانسی بود که او چتر آورده بود، چون آن بعدازظهر باران شدیدی گرفت.
Few people are as fortunate as him, having inherited a successful business from his family.
کمتر کسی به اندازه او خوش‌شانس است، چون کسب‌وکاری موفق را از خانواده‌اش به ارث برده است.
miniContext: Someone who is fortunate experiences good luck or favorable circumstances, often without having done anything special to deserve it. It feels fortunate to escape an accident unharmed or to land a job offer right when you need it most. People often count themselves fortunate when comparing their situation to someone less lucky, recognizing how much chance plays a role in life. While hard work matters, being fortunate can make a real difference in how smoothly things turn out.

examples: The temple is considered a sacred place where visitors must remove their shoes before entering.
این معبد مکانی مقدس به شمار می‌آید که بازدیدکنندگان باید پیش از ورود کفش‌هایشان را دربیاورند.
Many cultures treat the family dinner as a sacred tradition that should never be interrupted.
بسیاری از فرهنگ‌ها شام خانوادگی را یک رسم مقدس می‌دانند که هرگز نباید قطع شود.
For the tribe, the mountain is sacred ground, and climbing it without permission is forbidden.
برای این قبیله، کوه زمینی مقدس است و بالا رفتن از آن بدون اجازه ممنوع است.
miniContext: Something sacred is considered holy or deeply respected, often connected to religion, tradition, or deeply held values. A sacred text guides the beliefs of millions of followers, while a sacred ceremony might mark an important moment such as a birth or a marriage. People also use the word more broadly to describe something they treat with extreme seriousness, like calling a promise sacred because breaking it would feel deeply wrong. Whether religious or personal, sacred things are protected from being treated carelessly.

examples: She had to revise her essay twice before her professor accepted the final version.
او مجبور شد مقاله‌اش را دو بار بازبینی و اصلاح کند تا استادش نسخه نهایی را بپذیرد.
Engineers decided to revise the building's design after discovering a flaw in the original plan.
مهندسان تصمیم گرفتند طراحی ساختمان را پس از کشف یک نقص در برنامه اصلی بازبینی کنند.
Please revise this paragraph so it sounds less formal and easier to read.
لطفاً این پاراگراف را بازبینی کنید تا کمتر رسمی و خواناتر به نظر برسد.
miniContext: To revise something means to review and change it in order to correct mistakes or make improvements. Writers often revise their work multiple times, cutting unnecessary sentences and clarifying confusing passages before publishing. Governments may revise a law when it no longer fits the needs of society, and students revise their notes before an exam to fix any gaps in understanding. Revising is rarely a one-time task; most good work goes through several rounds of changes before it feels finished.

examples: The startup developed an innovative app that helps farmers track soil moisture remotely.
این استارتاپ یک اپلیکیشن نوآورانه ساخت که به کشاورزان کمک می‌کند رطوبت خاک را از راه دور پیگیری کنند.
Her innovative teaching methods made even the most boring subjects feel exciting to students.
روش‌های تدریس نوآورانهٔ او حتی خسته‌کننده‌ترین درس‌ها را برای دانش‌آموزان جالب می‌کرد.
The company is known for its innovative designs that often predict future fashion trends.
این شرکت به‌خاطر طراحی‌های نوآورانه‌اش که اغلب روندهای آینده مد را پیش‌بینی می‌کنند، شناخته شده است.
miniContext: Something innovative introduces new ideas, methods, or products that are noticeably different and often more effective than what existed before. An innovative solution to a problem can completely change how an industry operates, the way smartphones transformed communication. Businesses invest heavily in research to stay innovative, knowing that competitors will quickly copy any idea that proves successful. Being innovative requires both creativity and the courage to try something that has never been done before.

examples: After college, she decided to pursue a career in environmental science.
پس از دانشگاه، او تصمیم گرفت شغلی در زمینه علوم محیط‌زیست را دنبال کند.
The police continued to pursue the suspect through several narrow alleyways downtown.
پلیس مظنون را تا چندین کوچه باریک در مرکز شهر دنبال کرد.
He has always wanted to pursue his passion for painting instead of working in finance.
او همیشه می‌خواسته است علاقه‌اش به نقاشی را دنبال کند، نه اینکه در حوزه مالی کار کند.
miniContext: To pursue something means to follow it, chase it, or work steadily toward achieving it over time. A detective might pursue a lead for months before finally solving a case, while a student might pursue a degree in medicine because of a lifelong dream to help people. The word can describe both a physical chase, like pursuing a runaway dog, and a long-term goal, like pursuing happiness or success. Choosing what to pursue in life often shapes a person's entire future.

examples: For someone so young, he handled the stressful situation in a remarkably mature way.
برای کسی به این سنی کم، او وضعیت پراسترس را به شکلی بسیار پخته و بالغانه مدیریت کرد.
A mature oak tree can live for several hundred years if left undisturbed.
یک درخت بلوط بالغ می‌تواند اگر دست‌نخورده باقی بماند، چند صد سال عمر کند.
Her parents were impressed by how mature she had become since starting college.
والدینش از اینکه او از زمان شروع دانشگاه چقدر بالغ و پخته شده بود، تحت تأثیر قرار گرفتند.
miniContext: Someone who is mature behaves in a sensible, responsible way that is typically expected of an adult, regardless of their actual age. A mature student might handle criticism calmly instead of becoming defensive, showing emotional growth beyond their years. The word also describes living things that have fully developed, such as a mature tree with a thick trunk or a mature plant ready to produce fruit. Growing mature often takes time, patience, and real-life experience that cannot simply be rushed.

examples: The jury reached a unanimous verdict after deliberating for less than two hours.
هیئت منصفه پس از کمتر از دو ساعت مشورت، به یک رأی متفق‌القول رسید.
It was a unanimous decision among the board members to approve the new budget.
این تصمیم اعضای هیئت‌مدیره برای تصویب بودجه جدید، تصمیمی متفق‌القول بود.
The committee's vote was unanimous in favor of building a new public library.
رأی کمیته به‌طور متفق‌القول به‌نفع ساخت یک کتابخانه عمومی جدید بود.
miniContext: A decision or vote is unanimous when every single person involved agrees completely, with no dissenting opinions. Reaching a unanimous agreement can be difficult in large groups, since it only takes one person to disagree for the vote to no longer be unanimous. Courts, committees, and juries often highlight when a ruling is unanimous because it suggests the decision was especially clear or strong. A unanimous outcome tends to carry more authority than one decided by a narrow majority.

examples: The charity received a generous pledge of one million dollars from an anonymous donor.
این خیریه یک تعهد مالی یک‌میلیون‌دلاری از یک اهداکننده ناشناس دریافت کرد.
During the ceremony, every new member recited a pledge to uphold the club's values.
در طول مراسم، هر عضو جدید یک تعهد را برای پایبندی به ارزش‌های باشگاه بیان کرد.
The politician's campaign pledge to lower taxes helped her win the election.
تعهد انتخاباتی این سیاستمدار برای کاهش مالیات به او در بردن انتخابات کمک کرد.
miniContext: A pledge is a serious promise or formal commitment to do something, often made publicly or in writing. Charities rely on pledges from donors who promise to give a certain amount of money, even if the payment comes later. Politicians frequently make a campaign pledge to win voter support, though not every pledge is kept once they are in office. Because a pledge is meant to be taken seriously, breaking one can seriously damage a person's reputation and trustworthiness.

examples: The tailor offered to alter the suit so it would fit him perfectly.
خیاط پیشنهاد داد کت‌وشلوار را تغییر دهد تا کاملاً اندازه او شود.
A single decision can sometimes alter the entire course of a person's life.
گاهی یک تصمیم می‌تواند کل مسیر زندگی یک فرد را تغییر دهد.
Engineers had to alter their original design after the materials proved too expensive.
مهندسان مجبور شدند طراحی اصلی خود را پس از آنکه مصالح بسیار گران از آب درآمدند، تغییر دهند.
miniContext: To alter something means to change it, usually in a way that modifies its appearance, structure, or outcome without completely replacing it. A tailor can alter clothing to fit a specific body shape, while a writer might alter a story's ending based on feedback from early readers. Even small decisions can alter the direction of someone's career or relationships in ways that are hard to predict. Altering a plan is often easier than starting over, which is why the word appears so often in discussions about adjustments and revisions.

examples: She is considered a pioneer in the field of renewable energy research.
او در زمینه پژوهش انرژی‌های تجدیدپذیر یک پیشگام به شمار می‌رود.
The early pioneers who settled the region faced harsh winters and limited supplies.
پیشگامان اولیه‌ای که در آن منطقه ساکن شدند، با زمستان‌های سخت و امکانات محدود روبه‌رو بودند.
As a pioneer of modern jazz, he influenced countless musicians who came after him.
او به‌عنوان یک پیشگام در موسیقی جاز مدرن، بر موسیقی‌دانان بی‌شماری که بعد از او آمدند تأثیر گذاشت.
miniContext: A pioneer is someone who is among the first to explore new territory or develop a new idea, method, or field of study. Historically, pioneers traveled into unknown land to build new settlements, often facing great danger and uncertainty along the way. Today, people also call scientists, artists, and inventors pioneers when they break new ground in their field, like a pioneer of space travel or digital technology. Being a pioneer requires courage, since there is no guarantee that the unexplored path will lead to success.

examples: The office allows casual clothing on Fridays, so most employees wear jeans.
این اداره در روزهای جمعه لباس غیررسمی را مجاز می‌داند، پس اکثر کارمندان شلوار جین می‌پوشند.
It was just a casual conversation between old friends, not a serious business meeting.
آن فقط یک گفتگوی غیررسمی بین دوستان قدیمی بود، نه یک جلسه کاری جدی.
He has a casual approach to deadlines that sometimes frustrates his more organized coworkers.
او رویکردی غیررسمی و بی‌خیال نسبت به مهلت‌ها دارد که گاهی همکاران منظم‌ترش را کلافه می‌کند.
miniContext: Something casual is relaxed, informal, and free from strict rules or expectations. People wear casual clothes when they want comfort rather than formality, and a casual chat feels much less pressured than a scheduled meeting. The word can also describe an easygoing attitude, such as someone's casual approach to planning that leaves little room for structure. Striking the right balance between casual and professional behavior matters a great deal in workplaces that value both comfort and respect.

examples: The company plans to expand its operations into three new countries next year.
این شرکت قصد دارد عملیات خود را سال آینده به سه کشور جدید گسترش دهد.
Metal tends to expand slightly when it is heated to a high temperature.
فلز معمولاً هنگامی که تا دمای بالایی گرم می‌شود، کمی گسترش و انبساط می‌یابد.
She wants to expand her vocabulary by reading one new book every month.
او می‌خواهد با خواندن یک کتاب جدید در هر ماه، دایره واژگانش را گسترش دهد.
miniContext: To expand means to grow larger in size, scope, or amount, whether referring to a business, a physical object, or an idea. Companies expand by opening new locations or offering new products, while a balloon expands as more air is pumped inside it. People also expand their knowledge or skills by continuously learning new things over time. Expanding too quickly, however, can create problems if there aren't enough resources to support the growth.
